author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Validate a PS2 widescreen patch without breaking the HUD
summary: Match the patch to the exact serial and revision, compare field of view rather than stretch, inspect culling, HUD anchors, FMV, scripted cameras, and rollback cleanly when one segment fails.
heroAlt: Official PCSX2 patch-management screen used to enable and identify curated per-game patches

blocks.text: Confirm patch identity before judging 16:9 output

A widescreen patch modifies game behavior, not merely the emulator viewport. The same title can have regional executables, greatest-hits revisions, or language builds with different addresses. Record the serial, executable revision, image hash, patch name, and patch source. Establish an unpatched 4:3 checkpoint containing nearby geometry, screen-edge objects, a HUD, and a scripted camera.
Never force a patch intended for a different serial because the title names look identical. A wrong memory write can corrupt game logic, saves, cameras, or stability beyond the visible aspect ratio.

items: The executable CRC and release identity matched against the patch record, with the personal disc hash stored privately.
A clean title profile with all widescreen cheats disabled.
Gameplay checkpoint containing HUD corners and geometry near both screen edges.
A cutscene or FMV reachable from the same in-game save.
The exact official patch record preserved for rollback and attribution.

blocks.text: Test field of view, anchors, and scripted content separately

items: 1. Cold-boot at 4:3 and capture the gameplay checkpoint, HUD, and objects just outside the central view.
2. Enable one official serial-matched 16:9 patch and select its documented aspect output.
3. Repeat the camera position and confirm that additional world is revealed instead of the original frame being stretched.
4. Pan toward both screen edges and look for geometry that vanishes because the game still culls for 4:3.
5. Inspect health bars, minimaps, subtitles, and button prompts for shifted anchors or widened artwork.
6. Play the scripted camera and FMV without enabling a second aspect cheat.
7. Reload a normal in-game save after a cold boot to ensure the patch initializes consistently.
8. Record every passing and failing segment before deciding whether the improvement is acceptable.

blocks.text: A patch can change projection or field-of-view math while the HUD and FMV retain original coordinates. That is why a wider gameplay screenshot is only the first test. Serial matching protects memory addresses; edge pans reveal culling; scripted content reveals assumptions that free camera play may not exercise.
Keep the patch only when normal play and fixed presentation segments remain usable.

items: 3D geometry gains correct horizontal view without stretched circles or characters.
Objects remain present during left and right camera pans.
HUD elements stay inside safe areas and retain their proportions.
Subtitles, scripted cameras, and FMV are readable and correctly framed.
The patch loads only for the intended serial after a cold boot.
The HUD or menus become horizontally stretched: patch or aspect handling is incomplete.
Geometry vanishes near new screen edges: document culling and return to 4:3.
Cutscenes reveal off-camera staging or broken cameras: treat the patch as unsuitable for full play.
A different region crashes or corrupts behavior: remove the non-matching patch immediately.

blocks.text: Remove patch state before restoring aspect

Disable the widescreen patch, close the emulation session, select 4:3, and cold-boot the original checkpoint. Remove any temporary user patch file for the wrong serial and verify that normal in-game saves load without the modified state.
A community patch is executable-specific software

Review provenance, serial coverage, and update history before use. Do not redistribute game executables or copyrighted data with a report; share only permitted patch text, metadata, settings, and user-created evidence.
